title: Arguably, the legal system is working as it should in a free society. Citizens can (and should be able to) challenge organizations on the basis of law. Judges can and should make rulings based on law. Appeals courts can and should serve as checks and balances on the judges. This is a feature and not a bug. It just might be inconvenient or “chaotic” when it affects consumers of an entertainment product like college sports. The NFL enjoys a relative judge-free environment because it collectively bargained rules. The NCAA has not.
summary:
Arguably, the legal system is working as it should in a free society. Citizens can (and should be able to) challenge organizations on the basis of law. Judges can and should make rulings based on law. Appeals courts can and should serve as checks and balances on the judges.

This is a feature and not a bug. It just might be inconvenient or “chaotic” when it affects consumers of an entertainment product like college sports.

The NFL enjoys a relative judge-free environment because it collectively bargained rules. The NCAA has not.

title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 16: - It was hard not to notice a little extra pep in Niners' practice today, likely due in no small part to the return of TE George Kittle (Achilles) and RB Christian McCaffrey (tightness). The Niners eased both back in, with Kittle only doing individual drills and McCaffrey taking about seven reps in team drills, including a handful of carries. A positive step for both in the mission to be ready or very close to it in Week 1. - I asked McCaffrey about his absence and how he approached it. He indicated it was all part of the plan despite outside concern: "Obviously when you don't practice, the way the media works now it's a firestorm," McCaffrey said. "Obviously when you don't practice, the way the media works now it's a firestorm," McCaffrey said. Our staff's done a great job of coming up with specific plans. And again, I feel great. I feel fresh, and it's good to be back out there."

- WR De'Zhaun Stribling and CB Deommodore Lenoir were both back in practice after missing Saturday with a shoulder issue. Lenoir (blue) and Stribling (black) were in no-contact jerseys.

- The only new name on the non-participant list was rookie DE Romello Height. He was seen Saturday moving slowly after practice, but it's unclear what he is dealing with at the moment.

- The full list of non participants on Sunday: 

Height, LB Nick Martin (hamstring), CB Renardo Green (hamstring), OL Austen Pleasants (knee), LB Jalen Graham, WR Wesley Grimes (hand), RB Zamir White (illness), DT Gracen Halton (ankle), LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (soreness/tendinitis), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), QB Kurtis Rourke (undisclosed/ribs), WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), CB Nate Hobbs (groin), G Robert Jones (calf)

Players on PUP: RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL)

- WR Mike Evans again took part in much of the practice but didn't go all the way through it. He stopped toward the end after running a deep route on a play that went to TE Jake Tonges. He seemed to be moving fine but clear he and Niners want to be cautious to get him to the regular season ready to go. 

- The best part of the practice? The back and forth between QB Brock Purdy and LB Fred Warner. They've had their fun in this camp going at each other but it kicked into another gear today. During practice, Purdy layered one over Warner to Evans for a big gain. Later, Warner broke up a Purdy pass intended for Demarcus Robinson then boisterously let the QB hear about it. Warner also delivered a big thud to rookie RB Kaelon Black to force an incompletion (or a fumble depending on how you saw it) that again had Warner crowing. Purdy then dropped back and ripped one down the middle to a streaking Deebo Samuel just out of the diving, outstretched arms of Warner. Purdy let out a yell that won't be repeated here but suffice to say it was message received by Warner. Moments later, Warner and Purdy were laughing and chatting behind the huddle. The chess match between the two has been a constant in this camp. 

- Another constant in this camp? Purdy's excellence. He had a hiccup on an interception thrown right to CB Upton Stout but it seemed there might have been a miscommunication on it. Other than that, the ball barely hit the ground. I had Purdy at 16-of-19 depending on how you view the pass to Black that was knocked out. That included a handful of strikes for big gains to TE Jake Tonges, a would-be deep TD to WR Jordan Watkins and more in rhythm dishes to Robinson. It's been Purdy's best camp and it's fair to think even he would agree. 

- Tonges has come on very strong the past couple of days, not just making catches but stretching the field a bit. I had him down for four more grabs today after another handful yesterday. Purdy has plenty of comfort with him. Fair to wonder if we'll see more multiple TE stuff in the offense this year given that. 

- We got some one-on-one pass rush drills today (perhaps the final time in camp?)... I'm a broken record but rookie DT James Thompson Jr. continues to look the part of a legitimate rotational player. He had convincing wins in this drill against C Jake Brendel and G Carver Willis. To me, the most consistently productive UDFA the Niners added this offseason... RT Colton McKivitz has just been so solid here and overall throughout this camp. His ascent through the years has been fun to watch. Completely comfortable in his spot... G Connor Colby had a nice rep against DT C.J. West. West got a strong initial push and Colby seemed to be on his heels but Colby did a nice job reestablishing his feet and sitting down to anchor to prevent any further push... Good stuff from Brendel against DT Alfred Collins, OT Enrique Cruz against Victor Dimukeje, DE Quinton Bell against Cruz and C Drake Nugent against DTs Evan Anderson and Sebastian Valdez. 

- Just a thought: Nugent has had a solid camp and looks like he's improved. Given Toth's concussion, I wonder if Nugent could be a surprise on the 53 as the primary backup C behind Brendel?

- Some defensive highlights today: nice coverage by CB Ephesians Prysock on a deep ball from Mac Jones for Jacob Cowing. Prysock was again solid in coverage later on a Jones throw for WR Will Pauling... Warner had the PBU against Purdy but also had a nice run stuff against RB Jordan James... Thompson got home for a would-be sack on Purdy... Stout's interception against Purdy would likely have gone for a long return, also... LB Dre Greenlaw had a nice PBU (and a near pick) on a Purdy pass for Evans... S Marques Sigle made a nice read and shot the gap for a would-be run stuff against Samuel... LB Larry Worth had a hit on WR Malik Turner that forced an incompletion... S Ashtyn Davis picked off Jones on a pass for Cowing, who seemed to be favoring his leg a bit after the play. 

- Stribling made a nice catch along the sidelines on a throw from Purdy on the second snap of the starters' reps in team period. Stribling seems to have a great sense of awareness along the sideline that has showed up a few times in this camp. 

- More work for James and Black today as they come back from injuries. Their fresh legs stand out but it sure feels like both have a chance to contribute. It's been easier said than done when it comes to resting CMC in the past but it's fair to say this is the duo with the most juice of possible 49ers backup RB options of recent vintage. And both are proving capable of doing more than just running the ball. They've been adept in the pass game both as receivers and blockers the past couple of days. That duo also got a couple of looks as a kick returner combo today. 

- Still no proclamations from anyone on the Niners about the LG competition. But with Jones and Pleasants not practicing, it seems Willis might get the job by default if no outside additions are made. We'll see where Jones and Pleasants are health wise next week. 

- That'll do it for today. Niners are back at it Tuesday, which I believe is our last fully open practice of this camp. Thanks for reading. Enjoy your Sunday.

title: Source: Texans signing All-Pro special-teams ace George Odum By Aaron Wilson The Texans plan to sign former Indianapolis Colts and San Francisco 49ers All-Pro special-teams ace George Odum following a successful workout Sunday, per a league source. Odum has recorded 204 career tackles, three interceptions and four forced fumbles in 108 career games, 12 starts and four forced fumbles) on Sunday,. They also worked out former Tennessee Titans, Las Vegas Raiders and Birmingham Stallions safety Hudson Clark, defensive backs Tysheem Johnson and former New York Giants cornerback Tre Hawkins III. Hawkins has recorded 45 career tackles, one interception and three passes defensed in 21 career games and four starts. He has also played for the Washington Commanders. The Texans worked out running backs Jordan Mims, Deuce Vaughn, Blake Watson and T.J. Harden. The Texans are thin at running back with Jawhar Jordan (strained hip flexor), Noah Whittington (ankle) and British Brooks (broken hand, surgery) sidelined. The Texans officially signed former Houston Christian linebacker Caleb Johnson and terminated the contract of reserve wide receiver Juwan Winfree. Texans rookie corner and Manvel graduate Collin Wright has been sidelined with a soft-tissue injury along with cornerback Ja'Marcus Ingram, who's recovering from a dislocated shoulder at practice. Johnson worked out for the Texans on Saturday. He has recorded 40 career tackles, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and has played previously for the Chicago Bears, Jacksonville Jaguars, Atlanta Falcons and Miami Dolphins. Johnson (6-foot-2, 227 pounds) is a former Southland Conference Defensive Player of the Yea who finished his college career with 278 tackles, 27 tackles for losses, 10 sacks and seven fumble recoveries. The Texans are shorthanded at linebacker with E.J. Speed out for the season with a torn quadriceps tendon and Jake Hansen still working his way back from an ankle injury. Hansen has been running on the side at practice. The Texans placed linebacker K.C. Ossai on injured reserve Saturday.

THAT WAS FUN. Let's call it the final 49ers' training camp practice with this morphing to in-season mode fast. Always fun when 2 future Hall of Famers return...

🏈Brock Purdy was again dominant AND provided an intense/hilarious moment... we're not allowed to quote what players yell on-field but Purdy very pointedly let Fred Warner know that he'd beaten the defense after hitting Deebo Samuel on a crosser late. The two laughed it off after
🏈CMC was back in team drills — looked fast and fresh. He'd looked great earlier in camp too and said it was the preservation plan all along for him to skip about two weeks mid-camp

🏈Jordan James is running well in his return from the broken rib. Hit the corner for what could've been a long TD against the second-team defense
🏈"Long-term vision" moment for the 49ers' defense when long-armed rookies Ephesians Prysock and Larry Worth completely blanketed Malik Turner on a PBU
🏈I really think undrafted DT James Thompson Jr. is making this team

title: ESPN sources: The Browns are placing starting DE Alex Wright on season-ending injured reserve with a ruptured Achilles, and they now will sign former first-round pick DE Derek Barnett.
